## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;The innermost layer of the EVA suit. Provides thermal control&#10;&#9;&#9;by circulating air and water cooled by a sublimator over crew member&#39;s&#10;&#9;&#9;body. Can handle peak loads of up to 500 kcal/hr for 15 minutes, &#10;&#9;&#9;400 kcal/hr for up to an hour, or 250 kcal/hr for up to 7 hours.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Tubing Composition&#10;&#9;&#9;Woven into the fabric is a network of approximately 300 feet (91 meters) &#10;&#9;&#9;of flexible tubing used to circulate cooling water&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC): A synthetic plastic polymer $(-CH_2-CHCl-)_n$ &#10;&#9;&#9;chosen for its flexibility, durability, and ability to maintain shape &#10;&#9;&#9;under pressure while conducting heat efficiently. &#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;Polyurethane: In newer iterations, such as the Axiom Extravehicular &#10;&#9;&#9;Mobility Unit (AxEMU) developed for the Artemis program, the tubing is &#10;&#9;&#9;specified as medical-grade polyurethane plastic, offering enhanced &#10;&#9;&#9;biocompatibility and flexibility. &#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;
